newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner says to restructure energy units.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner says to restructure energy units.

text.p: Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group Kvaerner ASA said on Wednesday the board of Kvaerner Energy had approved a restructuring plan for the group's hydropower operations.
"The new structure will strengthen the group's hydropower operations," a statement said.

"Kvaerner is to spend $30 million on expanding Kvaerner Energy's facility at Sorumsand, north of Oslo, and on new engineering offices in the same area. These changes will mainly be carried out within the next 12-18 months."
A new hydropower laboratory will also be built as part of the new commitment, replacing the group's current hydropower laboratories in Finland, Sweden and in Trondheim, Norway, it said.
The thermal-power project organisation will move from Lodalen to Kvaerner's technology centre at Lysaker.

The assembly of gas turbines and equipment for oil and gas operations, which has until now taken place at Lodalen, is to move to Kvaerner Eureka at Tranby, south of Oslo. This move will not take place until the summer of 1998 at the earliest.
This plan will be put before the corporate assembly for approval on June 20, Kvaerner said. --Oslo newsroom +47 22 42 50 41
